title: aarch64: UBI offline overlay, kernel-mod reprovision hooks, and Terraform registry ACLs
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Adds UBI-based overlay for aarch64 air-gapped images, kernel module reprovisioning hooks for offline upgrades, and Terraform support for private-registry ACL provisioning. Includes smoke test and signed lockfile for offline bundles.
description: Context and motivation: Customers running private deployments on aarch64 hardware reported failures when performing upgrades in strict air-gapped environments where vendor kernel modules and UBI overlay layers were not present in the offline bundle. This PR adds an opinionated UBI overlay tailored for aarch64, an offline reprovisioning hook for kernel-module assets, Terraform helpers to provision registry ACL metadata for mirror endpoints, and Helm/installer tweaks to wire the components together. Summary of changes: Commit 1: add aarch64/ubi-overlay/ layout and package metadata (manifest.json + provenance), Commit 2: implement reprovision hook that runs during offline runtime upgrade to inject vendor kernel modules into the runtime squashed overlay, Commit 3: terraform/modules/registry-acl: new module to create mirror ACL objects (signed metadata) and provider examples, Commit 4: installer/helm: values and chart template changes to mount overlay and trigger hook, Commit 5: tests: add a lightweight smoke test that verifies overlay mount and module presence on aarch64 QEMU image. Files changed (high level): - aarch64/ubi-overlay/manifest.json and layer contents (added vendor-modules.tar.gz, overlay metadata), - installer/helm/templates/overlay-configmap.yaml (new), installer/hooks/reprovision-kmods.sh (new executable), - terraform/modules/registry-acl/main.tf and examples/README.md (new), - scripts/make-offline-bundle.sh (update to include signed lockfile and manifest checks), - tests/smoke/aarch64-overlay-smoke.sh (new). Testing and CI: Ran full CI on main with the new smoke test included; initial CI run failed due to missing gpg key verification in bundle script; fix pushed and CI rerun passed. The final pipeline: unit tests (pass), lint (pass), bundle-build (pass), smoke (pass). Security and provenance: offline bundles are now signed with our repository key and carry a SHA256 lockfile; terraform module includes an optional signed-metadata output for registry mirrors to be consumed by the installer. Upgrade/rollback behavior: reprovision hook is idempotent and adds a reversible marker file (/var/lib/redwood/overlay-reprovisioned). The helm chart includes a rollbackCleanupJob that removes injected modules on chart rollback to avoid cruft and kernel mismatches. Backwards compatibility: installer remains compatible with existing x86_64 bundles; the aarch64 overlay is only selected when node architecture matches and a new helm value 'overlay.aarch64.enabled=true' is set. Review discussion (high level): - Ethan: "Can we avoid extracting vendor-modules into rootfs on first boot? Security concern about unsigned modules." Response (Marisol): "We only materialize modules from signed archive verified against the lockfile; signature check added to hook." - Lena: "Terraform module needs clearer IAM example for S3-style mirror ACLs." Response: "Added example and documented minimal IAM policy in examples/README.md." - Rahul: "Smoke test should run under QEMU user-mode; CI job looks heavy." Response: "Kept test lightweight and gated behind matrix option; added a fast-local tag so CI can skip on PRs marked non-blocking." Approvals and merge: After two rounds of fixes and a successful CI rerun, reviewers approved and I squashed commits into a single merge commit. Merge method: squash and merge. Related work: ENG-8972 tracks aarch64 upgrade incidents; OPS-423 requested registry ACL automation for partner mirrors. Migration notes: Operators upgrading an existing private deployment should rebuild their offline bundle using scripts/make-offline-bundle.sh and set helm value overlay.aarch64.enabled=true for affected clusters. Additional notes: I left detailed implementation comments in installer/hooks/reprovision-kmods.sh and added a troubleshooting section to docs/private/airgap-aarch64.md. If you want a follow-up, I can split the terraform module into a separate repo to make it consumable by ops teams outside of the installer repository.
